name: What pool renovation issues are common in older Los Angeles homes?

mainEntity.name: What problems usually show up when renovating older pools in Los Angeles?
mainEntity.text: What problems usually show up when renovating older pools in Los Angeles?

acceptedAnswer.text: Older pools in Los Angeles often have a mix of cosmetic wear and hidden system problems. Common issues include cracked or hollow shell areas, outdated plumbing, old electrical components, failing joints, loose coping, deteriorated tile, and past patch repairs that no longer hold. Some properties also have access limitations, older deck tie-ins, or drainage problems that affect the renovation scope. When a pool is drained and stripped down, more issues can appear than were visible from the surface. That is why older pools often benefit from a more thorough evaluation before a quote is finalized. Homeowners should expect the possibility of structural or mechanical repairs and ask the contractor how those changes will be priced if discovered mid-project. A realistic renovation plan for an older pool should include some flexibility for hidden conditions rather than assuming everything below the surface is sound.
acceptedAnswer.description: Older Los Angeles pools often reveal cracked shells, outdated plumbing, worn electrical systems, failing tile, loose coping, and hidden leaks during renovation. Soil movement, age, and previous repairs can make the project more complex than it first appears.
